title: Sketch-Gated Trace Clustering for Accelerating Inter-Trace Redundancy Pruning

contributions.purpose: Reduce the expensive judge-model comparisons that bottleneck inter-trace redundancy pruning in parallel test-time scaling.
contributions.mechanism: Sketch-Gated DeepPrune adds a lightweight locality-sensitive hashing layer: compute 64-bit SimHash signatures from trace suffixes and use LSH banding to identify candidate similar clusters in constant time, gating an adaptive comparison budget (reduced from 10 to 3 when candidates exist).
contributions.evaluation: Method-level; efficiency payoff quantified in C2.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce Sketch-Gated DeepPrune, which combines SimHash suffix signatures with LSH banding to accelerate inter-trace redundancy pruning.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate the method reduces judge-comparison cost without hurting accuracy.
contributions.mechanism: Benchmark Sketch-Gated DeepPrune against DeepPrune on reasoning tasks measuring judge prompt count and accuracy.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 1.82x judge prompt reduction (1635 to 897) with zero accuracy loss compared to DeepPrune on AIME and GPQA.
contributions.source_quote: On AIME and GPQA benchmarks, Sketch-Gated achieves 1.82x judge prompt reduction (1635->897) with zero accuracy loss compared to DeepPrune.

contributions.purpose: Diagnose the actual source of the observed efficiency gains via ablation.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation studies isolating the adaptive K1 comparison-budget mechanism from the LSH candidate-filtering quality.
contributions.evaluation: Ablations reveal the prompt reduction primarily stems from the adaptive K1 mechanism rather than LSH candidate quality, suggesting simpler gating strategies may achieve similar benefits.
contributions.domain: Ablation analysis of the proposed mechanism
contributions.source_quote: Through ablation studies, we reveal that the prompt reduction primarily stems from the adaptive K1 mechanism rather than LSH candidate quality, providing insights for future efficiency improvements.

self_declared_provenance.quote: DeepPrune (Tu et al., 2025) addresses this redundancy through inter-trace clustering... We propose Sketch-Gated DeepPrune, which adds a lightweight locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) layer to filter candidate clusters before expensive judge comparisons.

DeepPrune (Tu et al. 2025) introduces inter-trace redundancy pruning through greedy clustering with a trained judge model... Our method builds on DeepPrune by adding a lightweight SimHash-LSH filtering layer that reduces the number of expensive judge comparisons while preserving clustering accuracy.

DeepPrune (Tu et al., 2025) addresses this by training a judge model J_theta that predicts whether two trace prefixes will yield identical final answers, and using it within a greedy clustering algorithm.

notes: Self-undermining ablation result: the paper's headline mechanism (SimHash+LSH candidate filtering) is shown by its own ablations NOT to be the primary source of the reported 1.82x speedup; gains attributed instead to the adaptive K1 comparison-budget gating. C2 reports zero accuracy loss (a tie/no-degradation result on accuracy).
